elements.element: Customer has no obligation to use Vendor exclusively.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly appoints Vendor on a “non-exclusive” basis, and Section 12.3 confirms that nothing restricts Customer from engaging any supplier and that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to use Vendor as its sole supplier.
elements.evidence: The prior “sole” provider language has been removed. Section 12.3 also preserves Customer’s right to engage any supplier.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it applies only to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the operative provisions impose no exclusivity and expressly permit Customer to engage any supplier.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because no exclusivity obligation is imposed, notwithstanding the provider appointment continuing throughout the term.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer has no exclusivity obligation requiring termination.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, it ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer has no exclusivity obligation requiring termination.

result.reason: The operative redline removes the sole-and-exclusive appointment and replaces it with a non-exclusive appointment, consistent with Section 12.3. It therefore reaches the preferred position through a minimal change while preserving Vendor’s appointment and avoiding any contradiction. The fallback protections are also satisfied because their exclusivity condition is demonstrably absent.
